name: go-indep-4
requirements: semver/semver.go: Parse(s string) (Version, error) accepts exactly SemVer 2.0.0 syntax and returns an error for anything else: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH decimal numbers that fit in uint64, then an optional -prerelease and an optional +build, each a dot-separated list of nonempty identifiers made only of ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Core numbers and all-digit prerelease identifiers have no leading zeros (build identifiers may). Nothing may precede or follow the version, not even spaces. Pre and Build hold the identifiers in order. String() returns MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, then -Pre and +Build joined with dots when nonempty, so it round-trips every valid input. Compare(a, b) returns -1, 0 or 1 by SemVer precedence: core numbers numerically; a version with a prerelease ranks below the same version without one; prerelease identifiers compare left to right, all-digit ones numerically and below any others, others in ASCII byte order; if every shared identifier is equal, the longer list ranks higher. Build metadata never affects Compare.

ini/ini.go: Parse(text string) (File, error). Lines are separated by \n, and spaces, tabs and \r are trimmed from both ends of every line. A line ending in a backslash continues: drop the backslash and join the trimmed text before it to the next trimmed line with one space, repeatedly; the joined line has the first line's number. Skip blank lines and lines starting with ; or # (there are no inline comments). A line starting with [ must end with ] and names a section (trimmed, nonempty); keys before any header belong to section "". Every other line is key = value, split at the first =, with the key (nonempty) and value trimmed. A value starting with a double quote must end at its closing quote: the quotes are removed, inner spaces kept, and \" and \\ are the only escapes. A repeated key replaces the earlier value, and a repeated header continues that section. Names are case-sensitive. The result has an entry for every header seen, even with no keys, and for section "" only when it has keys. Any other line, an empty name or key, a bad escape, an unterminated quote or text after the closing quote fails with a *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number.

textwrap/textwrap.go: Wrap(text string, width int) []string wraps greedily, counting runes, not bytes. Blank lines (only whitespace) separate paragraphs: leading and trailing blank lines are dropped, and consecutive paragraphs are separated by exactly one "" line. Within a paragraph, words are maximal runs of non-whitespace; whitespace, newlines included, only separates them. Each line takes as many words as fit, joined by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space. A word longer than width starts a new line and is cut into width-rune pieces; its last piece may be followed by more words. Text with no words gives no lines, and width < 1 counts as 1. Fill joins Wrap's lines with \n. Indent(text, prefix string) adds prefix to every line that contains non-whitespace; other lines and all newlines are unchanged. Dedent(text string) removes the longest run of spaces and tabs (compared byte for byte) that starts every line containing non-whitespace, and empties whitespace-only lines while keeping their newlines.

ratelimit/ratelimit.go: a token bucket. New(rate float64, burst int, clock Clock) starts full with burst tokens (burst < 0 counts as 0) and reads clock.Now(). Before every method the bucket earns rate tokens per second of clock time since its last reading, fractions included, capped at burst; rate <= 0 earns nothing, and a clock earlier than the last reading earns nothing and does not move the reading back. AllowN(n) takes n tokens and returns true if n is at most the tokens held; otherwise it takes nothing and returns false. n < 0 is always false, and AllowN(0) is always true. Allow is AllowN(1). Tokens returns the current, possibly fractional, count without taking any. Delay(n) returns 0 if AllowN(n) would succeed now; -1 if it never can (n < 0, n > burst, or too few tokens and rate <= 0); otherwise the wait until enough tokens are earned, rounded up to a whole nanosecond. SetRate earns at the old rate up to now, then switches rate. SetBurst earns up to now, then sets the size (negative counts as 0) and drops tokens above it; it adds none.

allocation.A: semver/semver.go and ini/ini.go, with focused tests.
allocation.B: textwrap/textwrap.go and ratelimit/ratelimit.go, with focused tests.

dependencies: The units share no types, imports or files.
